headline: All seven majors sit below their 200-day lines while whales quietly move coin off exchanges and funding stays cheap
paragraphs: Start with the regime, because it is uniform today: BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP, BNB, DOGE and ADA are all trading below their 200-day moving averages, and none carries a golden cross. BTC sits 49.1% off its 124,739.81 twelve-month high at 63,535.36, ETH is 60.9% off its high, and the smaller names are further still: SOL -69.4%, XRP -69.3%, BNB -53.3%, DOGE -75.6%, ADA -81.1%. Seven for seven under trend is a clean signal rather than a mixed one. It does not by itself say what happens next, but it frames everything that follows.

Momentum tells a more layered story. RSI-14 readings across the board sit in the mid-range, 36.2 on XRP up to 64.4 on BNB, with nothing pinned at an extreme in either direction, so this looks like a resting tape rather than an accelerating one. The MACD split is the interesting detail: SOL, BNB and DOGE show MACD above signal even while priced below their 200-day lines, a short-term momentum lift inside a longer downtrend. BTC, ETH, XRP and ADA show MACD below signal, more consistent with the broader picture. Worth noting too that 30-day changes are not uniformly negative: BTC is up 8.48%, ETH up 20.14%, BNB up 11.99%, ADA up 26.5% over that window, even as all remain under trend. Trend and recent price action are not telling quite the same story.

Positioning adds texture. Funding is modest, not expensive: 11% annualized on BTC, ETH, XRP and DOGE, just 2.4% on SOL, meaning the cost to hold a long perp position is low across the board, not the kind of crowded, costly setup that tends to get fragile. Yet the long/short account ratios lean long everywhere, and heavily so in places: DOGE 4.93, XRP 3.33, SOL 2.22, BTC 1.85, ETH 1.73. Accounts are skewed long under a market that is priced below its own trend line. Liquidations over the past day split by asset: BTC longs took $2.42M in liquidations against $1.19M for shorts, but ETH flipped the other way, $5.88M in short liquidations versus $3.89M for longs. Two majors, two different sides paying the price.

On flows, whale wallets moved a net $310.4M off exchanges over the last 48 hours, with BTC contributing $254.3M and ETH $56.2M of that. But the four-session weekly series behind it swings hard rather than trending: -$215.4M, then +$1,209.4M, then +$1,209.3M, then -$777.1M. That is oscillation, not a persistent direction, and the word 'trend' does not fit it. The single biggest moves were a Kraken BTC outflow of $128.9M and an Okex BTC outflow of $73.5M, alongside a large stablecoin shuffle at Bitfinex ($169.9M USDT out, $140.0M in). Stablecoin buying power sits slightly negative at -$29.9M, and the total stablecoin float is down 0.98% over 30 days, so the dry powder pool has shrunk a touch rather than grown. On the ETF side, BTC funds took in $7.8M on 11 Aug (only one same-direction day) but the five-session net is a positive $346.9M; ETH funds saw a small -$1.7M outflow on 11 Aug with two same-direction days and a five-session net of +$186.2M.

Sentiment closes the loop and it disagrees with parts of the flow picture. The Fear & Greed gauge reads 27, Fear, sitting near the bottom of its own 30-day range of 22 to 33. That crowd mood sits awkwardly next to whale coin moving off exchanges and a positive five-session ETF net on both BTC and ETH: money at the margin has not been uniformly defensive even while the sentiment reading says fear. What to watch from here: whether BTC or ETH reclaim their 200-day lines, whether funding flips negative (a sign shorts are paying to hold, not longs), whether the weekly whale net flow strings together same-direction sessions instead of oscillating, and whether ETF same_direction_days extends past one or two sessions in either direction.
